Recently, President Donald Trump caused quite a stir on both sides of the border by threatening to “annex” Canada over its trade policies and alleged illegal drug smuggling.

Unprecedented!!!  Well, not exactly. Marijuana prohibition really does cause long term memory loss.

Posted May 14, 2002: “The DEAland Threat to Canadian Sovereignty. DEAland Drug Czar Wannabee Threatens Canada with (Trade?) War Over Cannabis Policies. No More Mr. Nice Country!”

Twenty three years ago today, Canadian politicians and media were outraged when an American drug warrior, Robert Maginnis, threatened Canada with possible trade sanctions, or even invasion.

Maginnis had a long history in Washington.

From 1998 See Opposition To Medical Marijuana Makes The Weirdest Bedfellows Yet At The Washington Post

But this was a bit much. Maginnis threatened Canada: “To antagonize government leaders and grass roots leaders because you insist on having a radical drug policy that we will not ignore in the long term, then its going to have adverse consequences and I hope we would be able to rectify it before it comes to blows.”

Yep. It really happened. The “radical policy” that antagonized our leaders was to allow sick Canadians access to medical marijuana, and the supposed flood of “BC Bud” pouring across our border.

BC Bud? See When I Say That Marijuana Prohibition Causes Long Term Memory Loss, The Story of “BC Bud” Is The Best Evidence.

So, President Trump’s threatening Canada may have been unwise, but it was not unprecedented.
